sources.title: Robin README.md
sources.locator: What Robin does; How it works; Control and safety
sources.finding: Robin is the current name for this repository. The backend uses Deep Agents and LangGraph, supports parallel threads and subagents, accepts GitHub/Slack/Linear input, and delivers PRs. Managed Deep Agents is required as shipped.

sources.title: Robin desktop/README.md
sources.locator: Overview; This Mac; Work mode; Install on macOS
sources.finding: Experimental Electron client supports Apple Silicon macOS Ventura or later. Bundled robin/oswe CLI and local bridge run tasks in checkouts or worktrees. Local runs need the app open; Changes shows a session diff.

sources.title: Robin docs/INSTALLATION.md
sources.locator: Deployment; credentials; optional tracking; machine callers; thread scope
sources.finding: Web dashboard and FastAPI share one deployment. Docker self-hosting still requires Managed Deep Agents. GitHub/Slack are required, Linear optional. PostHog and Segment capture are disabled without their keys. Shared Slack threads accept queued participant prompts.

sources.title: Robin docs/CUSTOMIZATION.md
sources.locator: Sandbox; Model; Tools; Workspace MCP servers; System prompt
sources.finding: Per-thread LangSmith Linux sandboxes, snapshots and local bridges are configurable. Models use API credentials or LangSmith Gateway. Workspace and personal MCP scopes, skills and repository instructions are configurable.

sources.title: Robin docs/reference/workspaces.md
sources.locator: Access; GitHub access; Sandbox identity; Dashboard
sources.finding: All signed-in users see all workspaces; configured admins administer all. Public/private thread visibility differs. Per-workspace membership and roles are explicitly deferred; repository routing is not credential isolation.

sources.title: Robin docs/reference/human-review.md
sources.locator: Requesting; Reviewers; Configuration
sources.finding: Feature-flagged Slack human review cards track reviewer sign-up, PR summary and GitHub links. Required-check failures, drafts, closed and conflicted PRs block requests; supplementary specialists are separately selected.

sources.title: Robin docs/AUDIT_LOGS.md
sources.locator: Capture policy
sources.finding: Only opted-in marked dashboard mutations and tool operations are persisted with verified actors. Read routes and arbitrary MCP calls are excluded; general arguments and payloads are omitted.

sources.title: Robin docs/MERGE_QUEUE.md
sources.locator: Native observation; Configuration; Human controls
sources.finding: Optional native merge-queue observer reads GitHub state without merging or dispatching tests. Custom smoke-validation configuration is operator-managed, disabled by default, and not permission to merge.

sources.title: Robin docs/reference/claude-code-sync.md
sources.locator: Guarantees; What a thread shows
sources.finding: Claude Code hooks mirror local sessions into private read-only dashboard threads. Mirrors cannot be prompted, steered or stopped in Robin; uploaded sessions can start a separate continuable thread.

sources.title: Robin README capabilities
sources.locator: README.md lines 41-62 (What Robin does; How it works), commit ae120fc
sources.finding: Robin builds, opens or updates PRs, uses subagents for independent work, monitors opted-in PRs with /baby-sit and reruns evidence-backed flaky jobs, and runs schedules. Work starts and continues from the dashboard, GitHub, Slack or Linear; cloud coding runs in persistent per-thread Linux sandboxes, LangSmith by default.

sources.title: Robin sandbox customization
sources.locator: docs/CUSTOMIZATION.md lines 22-63 (1. Sandbox; Who creates sandboxes), commit ae120fc
sources.finding: Each thread runs in a LangSmith cloud sandbox that Managed Deep Agents creates when the run starts, using the deployment's LangSmith API key; defaults are 4 vCPUs, 16 GiB memory, 128 GiB disk, a 2 h idle TTL and deletion 7 days after stop, all configurable. The isolation technology (container or VM) is not named. A bridged thread runs on its owner's machine instead.

sources.title: Robin Desktop This Mac
sources.locator: desktop/README.md lines 11-21 (This Mac), commit ae120fc
sources.finding: A This Mac thread is an ordinary backend thread whose sandbox is the local project; commands run with the login shell environment minus secret-shaped variables. It runs only while the app is open, is visible from web and other computers, but only that Mac can continue it.

sources.title: Robin Desktop worktrees
sources.locator: desktop/README.md lines 35-36 (New worktree), commit ae120fc
sources.finding: New worktree gives a local thread its own git worktree on a placeholder open-swe/local-<id> branch that the agent renames, so several local threads can run at once.

sources.title: Robin model credentials
sources.locator: docs/INSTALLATION.md lines 288-300 (Model provider keys; LangSmith LLM Gateway), commit ae120fc
sources.finding: The deployer sets at least one model provider key (Anthropic, OpenAI and others) or routes all model calls through the LangSmith LLM Gateway with one LangSmith key.

sources.title: Robin scheduled automations
sources.locator: docs/INSTALLATION.md lines 844-850 (Thread ownership and PR authorship), commit ae120fc
sources.finding: Scheduled automations run as system-owned threads on the backend, open PRs as the GitHub App, and do not need the creator's OAuth token.

sources.finding: Claude Code hook events are posted to Robin so each Claude Code session appears as a private, read-only dashboard thread; Robin does not drive the session.
